docs.purpose: Where an operator edits the tuning numbers the pipeline runs on - the platform-wide variables, the per-trade multipliers, and the scope-intensity grid - across three tabs. Edits are held as a draft until the operator presses apply, at which point a dialog shows exactly what is about to change; confirming saves the new values and then kicks off the downstream re-calculation.
docs.data_story: It reads nothing from the database directly. Every value arrives through 2 contracts: `/api/admin/control-panel/configs`, `/api/admin/control-panel/resync`. Behind those contracts, the data comes from `logic_variables`, `scope_intensity_matrix`, `trade_configurations` and `trade_sqft_rates`, and writes land on `logic_variables`, `scope_intensity_matrix`, `trade_configurations` and `trade_sqft_rates`.
docs.under_126: **REBUILD** — it drives writes, so a client decision has to be re-homed on the server before the projection can be honest. It renders through the FORM renderer (every field carrying its Spec 99 §3 ownership row as data, with a declared rollback), reading by reference: `/api/admin/control-panel/configs`, `/api/admin/control-panel/resync`. It owns no component of its own, so its `owns.components[]` is an empty array — a legal answer, written down.

versioning.why: Both contracts are called only from this feature folder, so a shape change lands in one commit; nothing external pins the payload.

inputs.why: The shell reads only GET /api/admin/control-panel/configs; no page file touches the database.

outputs.why: Apply sends the whole draft to PUT /configs and waits for rows_updated before the store leaves draft; nothing flips optimistically, and resync is fire-and-forget on top.
outputs.rollback: There is no server-side undo. The client-side undo is resetDrafts() before Apply; after Apply the only rollback is a second Apply with the previous values, which the diff dialog shows before confirming.

state.why: Layer 3 owns the edit: useAdminControlsStore holds draftConfig/productionConfig and computes the diff, on top of a Layer-2 TanStack query whose staleTime and gcTime are both 0 so the panel never shows a cached tuning value.

staleness.why: The configs query sets staleTime 0 and gcTime 0 so every mount and window-focus re-reads the live table — the page-level QueryClient default of 30s never applies to it.

session.why: classifyRoute gates the page, but this is the one admin pair in the shard where NEITHER route calls verifyAdminAuth — the only check left is the middleware presence test, which is explicitly not a cryptographic or is_admin check.

rls_class.why: logic_variables, trade_configurations, trade_sqft_rates and scope_intensity_matrix are none of the ten Class-A tables and are not profiles, so they are Class B by the §2 default: RLS on, zero policies, service-role only.

checks.why: Every store read in the shell is a single-field selector rather than an object literal, which is what keeps a 400-row tuning grid from re-rendering on each keystroke.
A failed apply must keep the draft and surface a toast rather than silently discarding the operator's edits; the control-panel UI suites lock the draft/apply/diff path.
DECLARED AND CURRENTLY FAILING: guards.session says admin but neither configs nor resync calls verifyAdminAuth, so the contract's real auth class is "any request middleware lets through".

errors.why: Mutation failures raise a sonner toast and keep the draft on screen; only a render-time throw reaches the sibling error.tsx boundary.

classes.ui: toast with the validation detail; the draft is kept

emits.why: The feature wraps captureEvent in its own four-name whitelist and fires it on adjust, discard, save-failure and resync; nothing writes a usage ledger row.

offers.why: An internal operator tool renders no sponsored placement; no offers/placements table is reached from any file it owns.

metering.why: Nothing here is billable or quota-bearing: no usage_events / ledger write is reached from this surface or its contracts.

config.why: The logic variables are this surface's DATA, not its tunables — it edits the table rather than reading a bound from it, so it consumes no tunable of its own.

sharing.why: Both contracts are called only from src/features/admin-controls; no other surface reads or writes them.

limitations.what: Both of this surface's contracts mutate or expose the tuning tables with no per-route admin verification
limitations.measured: Neither src/app/api/admin/control-panel/configs/route.ts nor .../resync/route.ts imports verifyAdminAuth; PUT /configs rewrites four tables and POST /resync spawns the whole permits chain behind the presence-only middleware check.

limitations.what: PUT /configs writes four tuning tables and POST /resync launches the pipeline with no admin_audit_log row
limitations.measured: The only admin_audit_log writer in src/ is src/lib/admin/admin-audit.ts:72 and neither route imports it.
limitations.check_id: none — no checks[] kind covers "an admin mutation writes an admin_audit_log row"; escalated per Spec 128 §4

limitations.what: Three of the six measured UI states have no member in the states[] vocabulary
limitations.measured: unsaved_changes, confirm_sync and saving are real render branches of the shell; the closed set offers only loading/empty/hit/miss/ambiguous/partial/degraded/error/offline/schema_drift/unauthorized/rate_limited/redirect/static.
limitations.check_id: none — vocabulary gap, escalated per Spec 128 §4

notes: Thin page: all behaviour lives in src/features/admin-controls/ (ControlPanelShell 173L plus 8 sibling components, 1070L total, and the useGetConfigs/useUpdateConfigs/useTriggerPipeline hooks) - outside src/components/, so excluded from files per the stated rule, which is why loc is only 51. A sibling src/app/admin/control-panel/error.tsx error boundary also exists (not counted). This page creates its OWN QueryClient at module scope rather than using the root provider, unlike the other admin tools. DISAGREEMENT (tree wins): src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:8 states verifyAdminAuth is the FIRST LINE of every src/app/api/admin/**/route.ts (Spec 33 Sec 5), and the routes this surface calls do not import it at all - the only gate left is the presence-only middleware check, which middleware.ts:108 itself documents as non-cryptographic. identity.owner is UNRESEARCHED estate-wide: no owner registry exists in the tree, so naming one would be an invention rather than a measurement. a11y.touch_target_min_px is UNRESEARCHED because its vocabulary (UNRESEARCHED or an integer >= 44) has no member for a desktop-only admin page that declares no floor.

measured_gate.why: classifyRoute('/admin/control-panel') matches the admin-pages arm via `pathname.startsWith('/admin/')` -> 'admin'.

programme.why: An admin surface that operates the PLATFORM (users, entitlements, security, tunables, pipeline health) rather than either product specifically.
